text.p: Children's Broadcasting Corp told shareholders it expects to sign a letter of intent by October 13 covering alliances with theme parks in Florida and in Los Angeles and with a children's cable television network.
Christopher Dahl, chairman and chief executive officer, said at the annual meeting its agreements would involve use of facilities and program development.
Dahl would not disclose the names of its potential new alliance partners.
Analysts said Children's Broadcasting, developing a national radio network targeting the preteen market, lost momentum in July when ABC Radio Netowrks Inc terminated an operations agreement.
On Friday, Children's Broadcasting filed suit against ABC Radio and its parent, Walt Disney Co, for allegedly trying to copy its programming format.
Dahl told Reuters his company also was in negotiations with Knot's Camp Snoopy, an amusement part in the Mall of America in Minnesota and expects to start broadcasting there in January.

In addition, the company expects to develop a science show with the Liberty Science Center in New Jersey sometime soon and is negotiating with comedian Rich Little to develop a children's show, Little Time Players.

Dahl said Children's Broadcasting's KPLS-AM radio station in Orange County, Calif. received Federal Communications Commission approval to go to 50,000 watts from 2,500 watts, making it one of the most powerful stations in the Los Angeles area.
